title: Creatinine Clearance by HPLC
author: Kumar Sharma
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8e9hth6
materials: All reagents are HPLC grade. All aqueous buffers are filtered through 0.22 micron filter. Tubing is PEEK 0.005 mm tubing with hand-tight connectors. • Mobile phase: 5mM sodium acetate adjusted to pH 4.1 ± 0.1 with glacial acetic acid (final solvent strength is about 15 mM after acetic acid is added. Mobile phase was degassed. • Column: Zorbax SCX, -- strong cation exchange, (Aglient, Wilmington, DE), 50 mm x 2.1 mm, 5µ particle size). Five micron in-line filter and SCX guard column placed in front of analytical column. • Temperature and flow rate: Column run at 45 ± 0.5ºC. at a flow of 0.30 ± 0.02 ml/min. Backpressure was around 900 psi. Runtime was 10 minutes. • Detection: UV (deuterium source) at 225nm (flow cell volume is 12 µl). • Injection volume: three microliters (3 µl) from auto sampler. Temperature of autosampler tray was 18 ± 0.5ºC. • Identification and quantitation: Identification by comparison of retention time to pure standard of creatinine. Average retention time was 3.654 ± 0.022 minutes. Quantitation was achieved by external standard ranging from 0.003 to 1.000 mg/dl by serial dilutions using a weighted 1/X² regression regression line (8-10 points). May also use Excel, Prism or any other software to calculate a regression line and compute the unknowns.

steps.title: Prepare cage components
steps.instruction: Lightly spray the metal mouse screen, mesh support grid, and conical mouse funnel with silicone spray; wipe off excess and let the cage sit on the bench to vent fumes before assembly.

steps.title: Assemble cage and collector
steps.instruction: Assemble the Nalgene Diuresis Cage (650-0322) according to the manufacturer’s instructions and attach either the 15 ml or 30 ml fluid collector, choosing based on mouse strain, size, and number.

steps.title: Add food and water
steps.instruction: Place food in the feeder and attach; provide autoclaved tap water (distilled water acceptable, deionized water not) in the water bottle and attach. For non‑diabetic mice, add 3‑5 % glucose or sucrose water; diabetic mice usually need only plain water. Verify all connections are secure.

steps.title: Introduce mice and label
steps.instruction: Place the mice in the cage, secure the top, and label the cage with each mouse’s ID number.

steps.title: Add humidity water
steps.instruction: Pipette 1.0 ml of water into the fluid collector to provide humidity inside the cage.

steps.title: Cover vent hole
steps.instruction: Label a 15 ml plastic centrifuge tube and place it over the vent hole in the top of the cage.

steps.title: Collect urine
steps.instruction: Allow urine to collect for 24 hours (or any other predetermined interval).

steps.title: Remove mice and record time
steps.instruction: After the collection interval, remove the mice from the cage and record the exact end time.

steps.title: Inspect and rinse cage
steps.instruction: Examine the bottom of the cage for dried urine spots. If spots are present, remove the collection tube and the conical funnel, rinse the funnel with a small volume of deionized or distilled water (or urine from the collection tube), combine the rinse with the collected urine, and measure or weigh the total volume into a clean tared vessel, recording to three significant figures.

steps.title: Separate urine from feces
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the urine to pellet any feces, then aliquot the supernatant into labeled tubes and freeze them.

steps.title: Clean cage
steps.instruction: Wash cages with mild soap and water, rinse thoroughly, and dry before reuse. Autoclaving is not required unless the cage no longer provides a barrier; avoid autoclaving to prevent plastic deterioration.

steps.title: Process blood clot
steps.instruction: Mix blood, squeeze any clot with a wooden applicator stick if needed, then centrifuge at a minimum of 3,000 rpm for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Label precipitation tubes
steps.instruction: Label enough tubes for the upcoming protein precipitation step.

steps.title: Prepare acidified ACN
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of HPLC‑grade glacial acetic acid to 10 ml of HPLC‑grade acetonitrile (ACN) to make acidified ACN.

steps.title: Add specimen to ACN
steps.instruction: Transfer 25.0 µl of plasma (or 5 µl of urine) into a tube containing 100 µl acidified ACN (maintaining a 4:1 ACN‑to‑specimen ratio; 3:1 or 5:1 ratios are also acceptable). Vortex for ~15 seconds, then place the tube in a –20 °C freezer for 15 minutes to precipitate proteins.

steps.title: Centrifuge precipitation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at a minimum of 10,000 rpm, 6 °C, for 10 minutes (maintain 4 °C overall).

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the clear supernatant (≈125 µl) to a new, clean, labeled 1.5 ml or 0.5 ml Starstedt tube, avoiding any pellet.

steps.title: Evaporate ACN
steps.instruction: Evaporate the ACN to dryness using a SpeedVac, Centrivap, or a stream of dry nitrogen; apply mild heat if necessary. This should take about 30 minutes.

steps.title: Reconstitute residue
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the dried residue to exactly 25.0 µl with filtered Mobile Phase (Solvent A) and mix to dissolve the creatinine‑containing residue.

steps.title: Load autosampler tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the 25 µl solution into Perkin Elmer autosampler tubes, cap with special slit caps, and centrifuge at 2,000‑3,000 rpm for 10 minutes using a swinging‑bucket rotor. Verify that the liquid contacts the bottom (the “V”) of each tube.

steps.title: Program autosampler
steps.instruction: Enter the vial positions and specimen IDs into the autosampler program; double‑check that the mapping is correct before starting the run.

steps.title: Run quality control
steps.instruction: Include a banked QC sample (pooled mouse plasma stored at –20 °C) in each HPLC run.

steps.title: Calculate final concentration
steps.instruction: Multiply the measured creatinine concentration by 5 (e.g., 5 µl of original urine taken up in 25 µl of mobile phase) to obtain the final reported value.
